title: Share the RV32M multiplier product
motivation: The ALU currently describes separate signed-signed, unsigned-unsigned, and signed-unsigned 32-bit products. These products can map to multiple arithmetic resources and increase LUT/DSP routing pressure in a core whose critical path already passes through forwarding and the ALU. A shared unsigned product can supply all four multiply results with small correction logic.

hypothesis.motivation: The ALU currently describes separate signed-signed, unsigned-unsigned, and signed-unsigned 32-bit products. hypothesis.hypothesis: Replace the three product expressions in alu.sv with one unsigned 32x32 product. Use its low half for MUL and unsigned high half for MULHU, subtract the sign-dependent opposite operand from the high half for MULHSU, and apply both sign corrections for MULH. This preserves exact RV32M results while reducing duplicated multiplier hardware and congestion, which should improve placement and Fmax without adding cycles.

title: Iterative divider off the execute critical path
motivation:
The measured worst path passes through forwarding and the EX ALU, and the
combinational DIV/REM operators are the deepest arithmetic cones selected
by that ALU. CoreMark's ordinary instructions need not wait for division,
so separating division from the single-cycle datapath should raise Fmax
without adding latency to common instructions.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the combinational signed and unsigned divide/remainder operators
with one shared radix-2 iterative unit. DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU hold the
instruction in EX until the unit returns a result; the pipeline freezes
fetch/decode during that operation while older instructions drain. Keep
the existing single-cycle multiply and base ALU paths. This removes the
long divider cone from the normal EX-to-register path while preserving
RV32M divide-by-zero and signed-overflow results. Keep the formal ALTOPS
stand-ins consistent so formal mode retains its existing arithmetic model.

title: Backward-taken branch prediction
motivation: The five-stage core resolves branches and jumps in EX, flushing younger work whenever control flow changes. CoreMark has tight backward loop branches and direct jumps whose targets are already encoded in the fetched instruction, so predicting these in IF can avoid repeated redirect bubbles without adding a predictor table.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Predict conditional branches with negative immediates taken and other conditional branches not taken, and predict direct JAL targets in IF. Carry the predicted next PC with each instruction and redirect/flush from EX only when the resolved next PC differs. This should remove most loop and direct-jump penalties while keeping the predictor combinational and table-free; JALR remains predict-not-taken and recovers through the existing redirect path.

title: Balance the EX branch comparator
motivation:
The current worst path runs from a register-file value through EX and the
redirect, fetch, hazard, and decode control back to the ID/EX register. The
branch comparison is on this feedback path. The earlier static branch
prediction attempt slowed fetch, so this targets the existing EX decision
cone without adding work to instruction fetch.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the branch condition's separate 32-bit equality and signed/unsigned
relational comparisons with one shared, balanced comparison structure in
EX. Compare four 8-bit chunks in parallel, combine their equality and
less-than results from most significant to least significant, then derive
signed less-than from the operand signs and select BEQ/BNE/BLT/BGE/BLTU/BGEU
from the shared flags. This should shorten the branch-decision-to-redirect
path and reduce duplicated comparator logic while preserving the existing
branch semantics and pipeline timing.

title: Bank the register-file read network
motivation: The current measured critical path starts at the register-file storage and ends at the ID/EX operand register. The two asynchronous reads use variable array indexing across all 32 registers, followed by same-cycle write bypassing, which creates a wide mux network on the path feeding decode. A banked read structure can keep selection local and reduce mux depth and routing pressure.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Restructure the 32x32 register file as four local 8-register banks for each of its two asynchronous read ports. Decode the low address bits within each bank, combine each bank's selected word locally, then select among the four bank outputs using the high address bits. Preserve x0 behavior, reset clearing, write-first bypass, and the existing single synchronous write port. This keeps the pipeline cycle structure unchanged while targeting the measured register-file-to-ID/EX timing path; the more localized selection should improve placement and Fmax.

title: Tiny dynamic branch target buffer
motivation: CoreMark repeatedly executes tight loops and function control transfers, while this pipeline currently redirects from EX and discards younger work. The prior static predictor put instruction decoding and target addition on the fetch path; a small PC-indexed target table can predict recurring transfers without that instruction-dependent logic.

title: Qualify load-use source checks
motivation:
The load-use interlock currently compares a load destination against both
encoded source fields for every following instruction. Immediate and
upper-immediate fields are often mistaken for register operands, adding
bubbles even when the instruction does not read those registers.

hypothesis.motivation:
The load-use interlock currently compares a load destination against both
encoded source fields for every following instruction. Immediate and
upper-immediate fields are often mistaken for register operands, adding
bubbles even when the instruction does not read those registers.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Qualify the load-use comparisons by the following instruction's opcode:
check rs1 only for opcodes that actually read rs1, and check rs2 only for
R-type, store, and branch instructions. This preserves stalls for true
dependencies while avoiding false bubbles on immediate, upper-immediate,
and jump instructions, improving CoreMark iterations per cycle without
changing the pipeline or the branch feedback path.

title: Use valid-only pipeline bubbles
motivation:
The measured critical path crosses EX branch resolution, fetch redirect
selection, hazard control, and the ID stage. Redirects and load-use bubbles
currently clear wide pipeline bundles, putting that control signal on the
data path to many payload registers. The register-file banking attempt also
regressed, so the next structural target should be the control fanout on the
measured feedback path.

title: Predict function returns with a small return stack
motivation: Conditional branch prediction and a tiny BTB previously hurt timing because they put instruction decode, target generation, or associative lookup on the fetch path. CoreMark repeatedly calls and returns from functions, and RISC-V link registers make return targets available from the saved call address. A small return-address stack can predict these indirect transfers with less fetch logic than a general BTB.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a four-entry return-address stack that records PC+4 when a direct JAL or JALR writes a link register (x1 or x5). In fetch, recognize canonical returns encoded as JALR with rd=x0, rs1=x1 or x5, and immediate zero; when the stack is nonempty, use its top entry as the predicted successor. Carry each instruction's predicted successor to EX and redirect only when the resolved successor differs. Push and pop only for valid, aligned control transfers as they advance from EX, so wrong-path fetches and instructions held by a memory stall do not train the stack. This targets recurring function-return recovery bubbles while keeping the IF logic to a narrow instruction check and a stack-top mux, with no branch target addition or tag comparison.

title: Dedicated registered memory address path
motivation: The best current design's critical path runs through EX arithmetic to a memory-side output. Loads and stores use the general ALU result even though their address is always the forwarded base register plus an immediate. That routes the effective address through the ALU's general operation selection logic.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Compute the effective address directly from the forwarded rs1 and the decoded immediate in EX, carry it in a dedicated EX/MEM field, and use that field for dmem_addr, alignment checks, masks, and RVFI's aligned memory address. This gives memory operations a narrow address path that bypasses the general ALU result selection cone; synthesis can share the same addition with the ALU's ADD result where useful. All existing validity, stall, and misalignment behavior remains attached to the same instruction.

title: Dynamic branch direction table
motivation: The core resolves conditional branches in EX, so a taken branch discards younger instructions. Static backward prediction and a tiny BTB have both regressed, in part because of fetch-path target and lookup logic. A direction-only predictor can learn each branch's loop behavior without storing tags or targets.

hypothesis.motivation: The core resolves conditional branches in EX, so a taken branch discards younger instructions. Static backward prediction and a tiny BTB have both regressed, in part because of fetch-path target and lookup logic. A direction-only predictor can learn each branch's loop behavior without storing tags or targets.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a small PC-indexed table of 2-bit saturating counters for conditional branch direction. On a cold entry, use the existing backward-taken rule; train the counter from every valid branch's resolved EX outcome, including not-taken outcomes. In IF, use a taken counter only for a conditional branch and calculate that branch's target from its immediate; otherwise fetch PC+4. Carry the predicted successor with the instruction and preserve EX recovery when the resolved successor differs. The direction table should learn loop exits while using less fetch selection and storage logic than a BTB, potentially improving CoreMark IPC enough to offset the remaining fetch-path logic.

title: Segmented carry-lookahead execute adder
motivation:
The current critical path runs from register operands through forwarding and
the EX ALU toward a memory-side output. A previous dedicated address adder
duplicated the ALU arithmetic and regressed timing, so the remaining
opportunity is to shorten the shared arithmetic path without adding another
datapath. A grouped carry structure can limit serial carry propagation on the
common ADD/SUB and effective-address operations.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the generic 32-bit ADD and SUB expressions in the ALU with one
shared add/sub datapath built from 4-bit groups. Use local group propagate
and generate terms to calculate inter-group carries in a balanced lookahead
network, with conditional operand inversion and carry-in for subtraction.
Derive SLTU from the subtract carry-out and SLT from the subtract result and
operand signs, reusing the same arithmetic instead of separate comparison
cones. Keep the existing pipeline and operation latency unchanged. This
should reduce the carry depth on the critical EX result path without
duplicating the effective-address adder or affecting branch prediction.

implementation_notes:
# Implementation notes

- Replaced the ALU's separate ADD, SUB, SLT, and SLTU expressions with one
  conditional-invert add/sub datapath. Eight 4-bit groups compute generate
  and OR-propagate terms; pair, quad, and oct summaries form the inter-group
  carry tree. Four-bit local sums use native addition.
- SLTU uses the subtract carry-out, and SLT uses the subtract result with the
  operand signs. The pipeline and operation latency are unchanged. The
  ALTOPS stand-ins select the same shared arithmetic cone and preserve their
  previous formulas. The real multiply and divider paths are unchanged.
- Deviations: used a pair/quad/oct prefix tree instead of a full parallel
  prefix array. This shares intermediate carries and reduces logic while
  retaining grouped lookahead.
- Concern: Gowin timing measured 47.754 MHz (15 logic levels, 2909 logic
  elements) for the final adder version. The recorded baseline metadata is
  51.145 MHz / 2855 logic elements. The reported critical path still crosses
  the ALU result mux on the way to the memory address, so this change did not
  improve the measured Fmax in the local run.
- Local verification: Verilator lint passed; `make test TARGET=bench` passed
  all 6 suites; `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench` passed both ELF programs.
  The final formal rerun passed all 53 checks.
lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-002-r5s1 (regression, -4.47%): Replacing native ADD/SUB with explicit 4-bit group carry-lookahead increased mapped logic depth and area while the ALU result mux remained on the EX-to-memory critical path, so inspect the synthesized cone before hand-structuring carries.
